24.46: 24.46 Yet doctrine. RABANUS. The writer of this work signifies that the book is mystical, and useful to read. For historically it teaches morality, and allegorically the sacrament of the faith.
24.47: 24.47 See, etc. The ecclesiastical teacher profits not only himself, but also others by writing and teaching: whence, They that are learned shall shine as the brightness of the firmament, and they that instruct many to justice, as stars for all eternity, Daniel 12.
25.2: 25.2 A man and a woman. RABANUS. Whence Paul, Husbands, love your wives, as Christ also loved the Church, Ephesians 5. We can take the spirit in the man, the soul in the woman, who if they agree in the fear and love of God, whatever they ask shall be done to them, whence: If two of you shall agree, it shall be done to them, Matthew 18.
25.3: 25.3 Three kinds. THE SAME. These can be transferred to the devil, etc., down to because he would not be subject to his Creator.
25.5: 25.5 Those things which in youth. He who in youth learns not wisdom, in old age has not its fruit. Whence, A slack hand has wrought poverty, but the hand of the strong prepares riches, Proverbs 10. But he who meditates in the law of the Lord will give his fruit in due season, Psalm 1.
25.6: 25.6 How beautiful. THE SAME. A hoary head becomes, etc., down to it is not lawful for them to be ignorant of the knowledge and wisdom of the law.
25.9: 25.9 Nine things not to be suspected, etc. With the heart we believe unto justice, but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation, Romans 10. There are therefore nine things not to be suspected, that is alien from every suspicion of falsity, which right faith begets in man.
25.13: 25.13 Wisdom. Which is to shun evil. Whence, And behold the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to depart from evil is understanding, Job 28. Hence it is that one is added over to the kinds of virtues.
25.16: 25.16 The fear of God. RABANUS. Because as the number nine is imperfect, etc., down to but let not the presence of God, which you embrace, and desire to enjoy forever, forsake you.
25.17: 25.17 Every wound. There is no greater grace than true joy of mind, nor greater wound than the sadness of a deceitful heart in idolatry or in heresy, because in its wickedness is all malice.
25.18: 25.18 And every wound. He sees the wound of the heart who understands the injury of his perversity, but he does not see who by penance does not correct.
25.22: 25.22 There is no head, etc. RABANUS. The wickedness of heretics compared, etc., down to therefore her cohabitation is harmful to all.
25.26: 25.26 All malice is short. All malice is small in comparison with idolatry and heretical perversity, because they sin not through the frailty of the flesh, but through pride of mind.
25.30: 25.30 If a woman have the principality. Historically he shows how harmful the principality of a woman is, etc., down to she will be contrary to the husband, that is to the Catholic teacher, by thinking perverse things and teaching wicked.
26.1: 26.1 Of a good woman. RABANUS. As before he blamed the wicked woman, etc., down to and in the future will rejoice in the receiving of rewards.
26.4: 26.4 Of a rich man. The rich or the poor coming to the grace of Christ with devout mind will forever enjoy the pleasantness of the vision of God, because God is not a respecter of persons.
26.5: 26.5 Of three. By these similitudes he calls those who are separated from the unity of true religion, that is Jews, pagans, heretics, and false Christians.
26.6: 26.6 The accusation of a city. The folly of fools. For as brute animals know not how to discern between friend and enemy, and between good and evil; so the foolish know not the distance between Catholic and heretical doctrine, but obey true and false teachers alike. Against whom it is said elsewhere, Immediately he follows her as an ox led to the victim, and as a lamb wantonly, and knows not that he is drawn to the slaughter, Proverbs 7. But the cunning of heretics deceives the unwary not with an open face but deceitfully.
26.11: 26.11 A drunken woman. He describes the habit of a harlot, who by motion of the body and motion of the eyes displays lust. Mystically, however, it signifies the heretic, who in pride of sense and eloquence of words boasts his fornication, that he may more easily attract lovers of novelties itching in the ears, who turn away their hearing from the truth and are turned to fables.
26.12: 26.12 The fornication of a woman. RABANUS. By these three he shows the curiosity of the human mind, etc., down to by the pride of life, when he added, You shall be as gods, Genesis 3.
26.16: 26.16 Shall make fat his bones. With charity, namely, whence: He that keeps my commandments, he it is that loves me, and shall be loved of my Father, and I will love him, John 14.
26.18: 26.18 A woman, etc. Because the wisdom of God imbues the souls of the elect, and grants them guard of the mouth and efficacy of work, nor permits them to turn from her, because everyone that is born of God sins not, namely by violating faith or charity: Because the seed of God, that is the word by which he was reborn, he has in himself.
26.23: 26.23 Golden pillars. Teachers shining with wisdom are set upon silver bases, when in holy Scripture they are distinguished by their preaching.
26.25: 26.25 In two. RABANUS. Wisdom marks, etc., down to or, the path of truth forsaken, follows the byways of error.
26.28: 26.28 Hardly is he cleared. RABANUS. The worst act, not an honest thing, is condemned. That merchant is to be abominated who through immoderate ambition burdens his wares more with perjury than with price.
27.1: 27.1 For poverty, etc., RABANUS. As in the midst. Here by comparison, etc., down to and in the future eternal punishment remains.
27.5: 27.5 As in the shaking of a sieve. THE SAME. As a sieve, etc., down to: Satan has desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat.
27.7: 27.7 As the dressing of wood. THE SAME. Every tree, etc., down to the cultivation of wood therefore in its fruit manifests its quality.
27.8: 27.8 Before speech. Because speech shows thought. As if to say: Let no one praise him whom he has not known by manifest signs worthy of praise. Speech, however, can be taken for good work, that we praise no one before proof of good works. Whence: Praise not any man before his death.
27.13: 27.13 In the midst. RABANUS. He teaches temperance and caution in speaking, etc., down to: But he that shall do and teach, he shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven, Matthew 5.
27.15: 27.15 Speech, etc. Because as their action is contrary to the good, so speech is prone to speaking evils, heavy to hearing.
27.17: 27.17 He that discloses. He shows in what friendship is chiefly injured, in the evil, namely, of betrayal, which loses faith, and does not keep the equity of friendship, and therefore dissipates charity.
27.22: 27.22 As a roe. The roe, a wild goat, so called as if taking steep places. The roes are called ibexes or birds, because like birds they hold high and lofty places: and dwell in heights, so that from their height they are scarcely visible to human eyes. These if ever they perceive the adversity of wild beasts or men: casting themselves from the high peaks, receive themselves unhurt on their horns in the branches of trees.
27.24: 27.24 To uncover, etc. RABANUS. He shows the inconstancy of manners of the betrayer, etc., down to: An apostate man, an unprofitable man, walks with a perverse mouth, winks with the eyes, presses with the foot, etc. Proverbs 6.
27.30: 27.30 He that does a most wicked counsel. Because he sees not that his day will come. For the heretic or schismatic thinks his sect better than Catholic truth: whence he deceives himself.
28.8: 28.8 Remember. RABANUS. He who fears God restrains anger or fury, and forgets not the covenant of God, who says: Forgive, and you shall be forgiven, Luke 9.
28.13: 28.13 A contention. Indiscreet action: whence, Be not over just, nor more wise than is necessary, lest you be astonished. Immoderate discipline therefore excites the heat of fury, and a bold speech the shedding of blood.
28.19: 28.19 The third tongue. Heretical doctrine, which agrees neither with the Old nor New Testament, and troubles the hearts of hearers, and going from nation to nation, stirs up sedition.
28.21: 28.21 The stroke, however. Worse is the destruction of the soul which heretics kill, than any torment of the body. Blessed is he that is covered. Blessed is he who consents not to heretics, and whose heart their eloquence does not subvert, because as he is alien from their malice, so he is separated from their punishment.
28.28: 28.28 Hedge in your ears. After he has rooted out the evil of the tongue, he turns to the doctrine of the hearer.
29.5: 29.5 Till they receive. RABANUS. The fear of God better cures such a disease. For he who fears God as ever present, intends to defraud no one.
29.10: 29.10 For many, etc. THE SAME. He marks those who wish to harm no one, but for fear of perishable things will not benefit. Against whom it is said: Lay not up to yourselves treasures on earth, Matthew 6.
29.12: 29.12 For the commandment's sake. Mercy is to be shown to all the needy, nor is charity of neighbor to be lost for avarice.
29.13: 29.13 And hide not. For he who sees his brother in need, and shuts up his bowels from him, how does the charity of God abide in him?
29.16: 29.16 Above the shield of the mighty, etc. Alms avails more against the darts of the enemy than earthly arms: because these beget doubtful victory, that most certain, that death may be swallowed up in victory.
29.20: 29.20 The grace of a surety, etc. The teacher, namely, who for faith and good works promises eternal life. This sentence reproves Pelagius who puts free will before grace, whereas the elect are freed by grace alone.
29.23: 29.23 He that has lost, etc. That is, he who keeps not the unity of faith and sincerity of the law, but is entangled in various errors.
29.27: 29.27 Recover your neighbor. He counsels that according to your means you afford comfort to your neighbor, and so provide for yourself that you fall not into the snare.
29.28: 29.28 The chief thing for life, etc. RABANUS. He teaches frugality, and hospitality and honesty, etc., down to and the Lord made coats of skins for the first parents after sin.
29.29: 29.29 Better is the life of a poor man, etc. Literally. It is better to take a slender living under a mean cottage in security, than to seek splendid feasts with weariness in uncertain places. THE SAME. Allegorically. Better is the life, etc., down to where is labor and superfluous care.
29.30: 29.30 Least. THE SAME. Let what you have suffice you, etc., down to a good name is better than many delights.
29.33: 29.33 Pass on. As: You who delight in another's hospitality, return to your own, and feed yourself and others by your labor. Seek not superfluous food from another's house. The reception of neighbors suffices you.
29.34: 29.34 The reproach. RABANUS. Mystically, however, the ecclesiastical man is admonished, etc., down to but in the future examination let him bear the eternal reproach of confusion.
30.1: 30.1 He that loves his son. RABANUS. He admonishes fathers both carnal and spiritual to instruct their sons diligently, that they live honestly, lest by wantonness they run about after the teachings of others.
30.8: 30.8 An unbroken horse. An unbroken horse goes to the precipice; an undisciplined son rushes into sin. He teaches therefore spiritual fathers to instruct and correct their sons; not to loosen the reins immoderately, lest they fall into the baseness of vices, and themselves bear everlasting disgrace.
30.14: 30.14 Better is the poor man. Sweet is the sleep of the laborer, whether he eat much or little. For the fullness of the rich does not suffer him to sleep.
30.15: 30.15 The health of the soul. The true health of the soul is justice, to which gold and silver cannot be compared, because riches will not profit in the day of vengeance. But justice will deliver the soul from death.
30.18: 30.18 Good things hidden. RABANUS. He speaks against those who hide the talent of the word; whose knowledge is useless to virtues, like feasts to the dead and a treasure.
30.21: 30.21 As a eunuch. He does not serve for the embrace of a virgin, so the adoration of an idol is unfitting and useless to those who adore.
30.23: 30.23 The joy of the heart. Because no virtue stands without it. But the greatest of these is charity, 1 Corinthians 13.
30.26: 30.26 They shorten the days, etc. Bloody men shall not live out half their days, Psalm 54. THE SAME. That is, the prosperity which they promise themselves they cannot have forever.
31.1: 31.1 The wood of offense. RABANUS. As Adam in the forbidden tree, etc., down to which shines with the splendor of eloquence, and seduces the curious.
31.12: 31.12 Upon the table. THE SAME. Literally, continence, etc., down to but let us hold the way of the holy teachers.
31.13: 31.13 Say not, etc. THE SAME. As if he said: Do nothing by presumption, nor before you learn put your hand to writing.
31.19: 31.19 Use, etc. As: Love sobriety, act temperately, and nothing too much, lest you fall into the scandal of confusion. It befits the Christian therefore before all things to love humility, to be cautious in reading Scripture, to hold right faith, to keep measure in knowledge, and the rule of charity, that he may be approved before God and men.
31.22: 31.22 How sufficient. A slender diet is useful to soul as well as body, but a superfluous one the contrary. A little wine. Spiritual wine also taken moderately is useful to body and soul: taken immoderately it makes mad, and separates from God, whence anxious care, and greatest disturbance, and perpetual torture.
31.24: 31.24 Sleep of health. Sleep is lighter on a small diet. Mystically, however, he who is sober in spiritual wine rests in the contemplation of truth until the morning of the resurrection.
31.25: 31.25 And vomit, etc. Physicians say that vomiting purges the stomach: lessens choler. Mystically, however, he who passes the measure and is burdened with carnal faults, let him vomit the foulness of sin by confession, and by chastisement of the body return to health.
31.27: 31.27 In all your works. He admonishes that we lose not time, that we work well, that keeping the commandments of God we may find rest for our souls.
31.28: 31.28 Splendid. Literally: he invites to alms: Because he who sows in blessings shall also reap of blessings, 2 Corinthians 9. Mystically, however, he who faithfully dispenses the bread of the word, and conceals not the testimony of truth, shall be blessed in the present and in the future.
31.30: 31.30 For many, etc. RABANUS. That is drunkenness overthrows many, which lessens the sense, stirs up anger, inflames lust, reveals the secrets of the soul.
31.31: 31.31 Fire. That is as fire softens the hardness of iron, and makes it glow, so wine inflaming the hearts of the proud impels to crime.
31.32: 31.32 Equal life. Wine drunk soberly does not take away the life of equity; but brings sobriety and the other adornments of virtues. Wine. It is plain that irritation, anger, and many ruins are born of drunkenness, and bitterness of soul, and wounds of crimes are multiplied.
32.1: 32.1 Ruler. RABANUS. He who presides in dignity ought not to be proud: He that is the greater among you, let him become as the younger, etc., Matthew 10.
32.7: 32.7 A little gem of carbuncle. RABANUS. It holds the principality among burning gems, etc., down to and venerates the mysteries of the Lord's passion with worthy sacrament.
32.14: 32.14 Before the hail. THE SAME. The flash of lightning will go before the weight of hail; so the splendor of grace before modesty.
32.15: 32.15 To the hour of rising. THE SAME. He admonishes that we be not sad, etc., down to who by grace made us and filled us with all good [works].
32.22: 32.22 A man of counsel. The more prudent one is, the more he uses the counsel of neighbors, to add understanding to himself.
32.24: 32.24 My son, do nothing without counsel. These can be taken of the Catholic and the heretic. For the Catholic fearing God does all things by the counsel of teachers and the instruction of the Scriptures. The heretic, trusting in his own wisdom, presses on with his own inventions: but when his folly appears, he will be convicted by holy preachers with divine sentences.
33.5: 33.5 The heart of a fool. RABANUS. As the wheel of a cart and the axle, etc., down to: The heart of fools shall be unlike, Proverbs 15.
33.6: 33.6 A horse, etc. THE SAME. As a beast of burden has no reason, etc., down to but through the offices of the mouth equally to both opens secrets.
33.7: 33.7 Why does one day. THE SAME. Because above he blamed the fool, etc., down to that they be for signs and for seasons, and days, and years.
33.8: 33.8 The sun made. THE SAME. God commanded in the law, etc., down to and chiefly that pleases which is done in order and reason.
33.10: 33.10 Of them he exalted. THE SAME. That is, by his discernment he distinguished those whom he rewarded for good deeds, and to whom he rendered a worthy reward for evil deeds. And all men. After the arrangement of the stars, etc., down to but the impious he condemned with eternal malediction.
33.13: 33.13 As clay, etc. RABANUS. The Creator holds in his hand the mass of the human race, etc., down to and whom he ought to harden according to justice.
33.15: 33.15 Against evil. The investigator of the works of God finds in them a certain contrariety, but wonderfully ordered by God. God therefore is not the maker of evil, who made all things very good; nor did he make death, nor does he rejoice in the destruction of the dead, but is the wonderful ordainer of the universe. Natures therefore are good, and are from God: but vices are not from God.
33.18: 33.18 Look. He admonishes all in common not to omit the reason of their right, because otherwise one cannot have peace and quiet. For he who loses the authority of his primacy puts himself into contempt and distress: but he who wisely guards his place directs himself and his own to progress in virtue.
33.19: 33.19 Hear. Literally he teaches fathers to rule their sons, and to bring them up with discipline, until they come to perfect age, that they may be worthy heirs of their fathers. Spiritually, however, he instructs the rulers of the Church to hold their dignity to the end, and to leave their well-nourished disciples as heirs of their labor. The rulers ought to hold outwardly what they undertake for the profit of others.
33.25: 33.25 Food and a rod, etc. RABANUS. It is necessary that wicked servants, etc., down to that they may have, namely food and clothing, not leisure to wander.
33.31: 33.31 If you have a faithful servant, etc. THE SAME. He gave the law of the good servant, etc., down to for it is not the man that is to be pursued, but the vices.
34.2: 34.2 Like him that catches. RABANUS. He signifies that dreams are deceptive, etc., down to that they may know what they receive from a good spirit, or what they suffer from illusion.
34.8: 34.8 Without a lie. Dreams cast aside, he exhorts that the doctrine of wisdom be believed, which planted in the mouth of a faithful man consummates the word without a lie.
34.9: 34.9 Will declare understanding. To the instructing of others: whence, Blessed be God, who comforts us in all our tribulation, that we also may be able to comfort them who are in all distress, 2 Corinthians 12.
34.10: 34.10 But he that in many things, etc. Changeable, namely in mind, is unstable in action. Or, he who, the unity of faith lost, follows the manifold sects of heretics, serves many impieties.
34.12: 34.12 Very many of words. RABANUS. He signifies Scripture; he who intently meditates Scripture, and humbly entreats the Lord, obtains knowledge of things and words.
34.23: 34.23 The gifts of the wicked. Very detestable is the sacrifice which is compared to the grief of a bereaved father. Some weigh how much they give, and not how much they seize. And they gather rewards, and put them into a bag with holes. In a bag with holes money seems to be put in, but not when it is lost. They therefore who regard how much they give, but not how much they seize, put the rewards into a bag with holes, because they heap them up looking to the hope of their trust, but not looking at themselves they lose.
34.26: 34.26 He that takes away. RABANUS. In the sweat of his face the poor man earns bread. He who takes it away violently is as one who kills his neighbor.
34.28: 34.28 One building. This is what he said above, that a sacrifice from plunder is not acceptable. He who offers from plunder seems to himself to prepare an edifice of virtues, and does not attend to the crime of avarice and plunder.
34.30: 34.30 He that is baptized. THE SAME. Wash yourselves, etc., down to and again commit things to be wept for.
35.1: 35.1 He that keeps. RABANUS. He prays well, etc., down to because by working well he keeps justice.
35.3: 35.3 Of propitiations. Between offering and sacrificing there is this difference. For he sacrifices who makes a sacrifice. He offers acceptably who makes a sacrifice and obtains what he sought by the sacrifice.
35.4: 35.4 Will repay, etc. Both, namely, that is pleasing to God, both what is offered on the altar in commemoration of Jesus Christ, and what is given to the neighbor through charity.
35.10: 35.10 With a good heart. THE SAME. Whatever is not given with a good heart does not merit grace with God. For man sees the face, but God the heart. And diminish not, etc. Mystically. The first-fruits of the crops, etc., down to by whom both the beginning and perfection of good work is given.
35.13: 35.13 Seven times as much. Perfect, namely, reward. For the number seven, etc., down to but also gives the operation of the four principal virtues.
35.14: 35.14 Offer not wicked gifts, etc. With God there is no quantity of gift; nor is the person of the mighty regarded: but love and humility of heart. Therefore a sacrifice ought not to be offered from iniquity, but from just labor.
35.21: 35.21 And till he draw near, etc. He looks to the above, affirming that the Lord mercifully hears the prayer of the humble, who cease not until they receive consolation.
36.1: 36.1 Have mercy on us. RABANUS. In the person of the faithful he directs prayer to God, to defend them and put down their enemies, that duly corrected they may again acknowledge God, and forsake idols.
36.7: 36.7 Glorify your hand, etc. THE SAME. He desires that the divine majesty through the hand and right arm, that is through Christ, by whom the ancient miracles were done, renew in the time of grace, that the God of the old law and the new may be understood to be the same.
36.15: 36.15 Lift up the adversary, etc. RABANUS. It signifies by the coming of Christ, etc., down to for the state of the Church and the salvation of the faithful.
36.16: 36.16 Sion, etc. The knowledge of Scripture, in which the unspeakable power of God is preached.
36.17: 36.17 And raise up, etc., All the prophets give testimony to the incarnation of Christ, that God made man should espouse the Church to himself.
36.19: 36.19 According to the blessing, etc. THE SAME. The order, namely, and rite of the priesthood, etc., down to what Aaron figured in temporal sacrifices, let him fulfill in the spiritual ones of the Gospel.
36.20: 36.20 Every meat. THE SAME. After he foretold the calling of the Gentiles, etc., down to so let us discern the true doctrine, and the false.
36.24: 36.24 The beauty of a woman. The grace of Christ, which by preaching heals souls, and softens the concupiscence of the flesh. This abounds in the Church, whose desire is above all concupiscence of man, because in her is the comeliness of virtues and the beauty of doctrine. Above all. No concupiscence of man can be compared to this desire: because, Favor is deceitful and beauty is vain; the woman that fears the Lord she shall be praised, Proverbs 31.
36.25: 36.25 There is not a man. Christ who exceeds human nature. Whence, Beautiful in form above the sons of men, Psalm 44. For he did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.
36.26: 36.26 A help. The help of the Church is according to the dispensation of Christ. Whence, My help is just from the Lord, Psalm 7., etc. He is the pillar of her infirmity, and the rest of her labor.
36.28: 36.28 He that has no nest. That is, the Church, where the souls of the elect nourish the children of good works. Whence, The sparrow has found herself a house, and the turtle a nest for herself where she may lay her young ones, Psalm 83.
37.1: 37.1 Every friend. RABANUS. Above he expressed more diligently the true friend and the false, saying: And he will not abide in the day of tribulation.
37.2: 37.2 But a companion. The true friend loves with all his mind, and profits by work. Whence, Let us not love in word nor in tongue, but in deed and in truth, 1 John 3.
37.3: 37.3 O presumption. He detests hypocrisy, when the wicked feigns himself good by covering dry malice, in which there is not the fatness of charity or mercy.
37.5: 37.5 For the sake of the belly. For gluttony, not for friendship. Heretics can be understood among false friends, who do everything rightly, as counselors of souls, though they are betrayers. Whence, Beware of false prophets, Matthew 7., etc. With the father-in-law. The father-in-law, who is a kinsman on the female side, shows a womanish and changeable mind, likewise also zeal which is chiefly of souls.
37.8: 37.8 Every counselor. He still teaches all caution to be had in taking friends and counselors. For many feign themselves friends and counselors, and lay snares. Whence Jeremiah, Let every man take heed of his neighbor, Jeremiah 9.
37.14: 37.14 Attend not. RABANUS. He enumerated different kinds of counselors, in which he marked several persons who disagree with truth. Whence he commanded that one not take counsel with such, whose counsel is perilous. The prudence, faith, will and religion of the counselor are therefore to be foreseen.
37.18: 37.18 The soul of a holy man. The diversity of counselors shown, he adds how much the knowledge of the saints infused by the Holy Spirit exceeds human wisdom.
37.22: 37.22 A man skillful. Because he had foretold concerning the tongue: he continues concerning good and bad teachers.
37.28: 37.28 The life of a man. THE SAME. The present life of men is not in uncertainty with him. Whence, The days of man are short, the number of his months is with you, Job 14.
37.32: 37.32 Be not greedy. According to the history, he praises frugality, blames surfeiting, which leads the devourer to sickness. Mystically, however, he admonishes that we be temperate in temporal things. Whence, You have found honey, eat what is sufficient for you, Proverbs 25., etc. And elsewhere: Not to be more wise than it behooves to be wise, Romans 12.
38.1: 38.1 Honor the physician. RABANUS. He wills us to be discreet, etc., down to both therefore are to be honored, but the spiritual preferred.
38.5: 38.5 Was not water. He touches an ancient history because in the desert of Sur the children of Israel found bitter water, but God showed Moses a tree, which cast in made the water sweet; where according to the history the medicine of the wood is shown to make the waters sweet. Mystically, however, the bitter water signifies the law, to which if the confession of the cross and the sacrament be joined, it is made drinkable.
38.7: 38.7 By these he cures. THE SAME. Against different infirmities, physicians apply different remedies, foods and drinks, plasters, and ointments: that the medicines may suit the diseases. Likewise spiritual physicians do.
38.10: 38.10 Turn away. Like that: Decline from evil, and do good. And from all, etc., and not only the body, but that you be innocent in hands and clean of heart.
38.11: 38.11 Give sweetness. The sacrifice of bread and wine offered in memory of the Lord's passion especially heals the wounds of souls and is very necessary not only for the living but also for the dead.
38.15: 38.15 Shall fall into the hands of the physician. THE SAME. Of sickness and trouble, etc., down to and earnestly beseech the Lord to direct their works, and give relief to the sick.
38.16: 38.16 Son, etc. Because he has discussed infirmities and the cures of physicians, he adds about the funerals of the dead.
38.21: 38.21 Remember the last things. THE SAME. An admonition of good fathers that their sons prepare for themselves provision of good works.
38.22: 38.22 For there is no returning. As if he said: Be cautious therefore in all things, lest perhaps at the death of a neighbor you grieve more than is right.
38.24: 38.24 In the rest. As: Keep the memory of the dying continually, and trust, and comfort him with hope, lest he fail at the last moment.
38.26: 38.26 He that holds the plough. It signifies holy preachers, who at every time by teaching, exhorting, instruct their hearers to draw out the virtue of the inner man, and reform the human soul to the image of God. Whence, As a wise architect I have laid the foundation, 1 Corinthians 3. And elsewhere: My little children, of whom I am in labor again, until Christ be formed in you, Galatians 4. As many kinds of virtues as there are, so many operations and instructions doctrine imprints on the minds of the elect.
38.28: 38.28 So every craftsman, etc. The order of preachers, who by diverse offices discharge their ministry, temper doctrine according to the hearers: who form the frail and infirm by words and example, that they may make vessels unto honor. He shall give his heart. When he shows to subjects the changeable conversation of the present life unchanged by the footprints of good works.
38.33: 38.33 In his arm. RABANUS. Because by many examples, etc., down to that in the furnace of the heart he may solidify the operation of disciples with the fire of charity.
39.15: 39.15 If he continue. RABANUS. Of Christ, whose members they are, they have all from him: who is the power and wisdom of the Father.
39.17: 39.17 Hearken to me. THE SAME. Understand my doctrine, you minds of the elect begotten through baptism, and bring forth the fruit of martyrdom in the course of mortal life.
39.20: 39.20 And with harps. THE SAME. Whence: Give praise to the Lord on the harp, Psalm 32. The harp is the concavity of the wooden belly at the bottom, etc., down to which according to the form of the psaltery come to us from above.
39.22: 39.22 At his word. THE SAME. When he gathered the waters, etc., down to or the water of persecution, is restrained by the dispensation of God.
39.24: 39.24 The works of all flesh. The presence of God precedes all things, and whatever is done in time is present to him without time. Nothing therefore is new, or changeable in his sight, Acts 1.
39.26: 39.26 It cannot be said, etc. He forbids us to be curious, and to search out what it is not fitting to know. For all things will be made manifest in their time, when the Lord will enlighten the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of hearts.
39.27: 39.27 The blessing, etc. As after the pouring out of the flood the waters returned, that dry land might appear and bring forth; so after the extinction of the impious, the elect are given the power of bearing fruit.
39.31: 39.31 The principal things necessary. Before the flood, by the fruit of the earth men were nourished with natural food, flesh not yet being granted.
39.35: 39.35 Fire, hail. RABANUS. All things obeyed man before sin; after sin the world fights against him. Hence famine and death, and a thousand perils of death, beasts also rage against him, and the sword of heavenly vengeance.
39.37: 39.37 In his commandments. Because according to the heavenly sentence, in due time worthy vengeance will lay waste sinners.
39.38: 39.38 Therefore from the beginning I was confirmed. He looks to the above, where he says: It cannot be said, etc. For he sees the incomprehensible judgments of God, and unsearchable ways, nor dares to say or write anything rashly thence: but discoursing temperately of these, he left not the cause but the manner manifest to the divine counsel.
39.40: 39.40 It cannot be said. He gives useful counsel, that we not incautiously discuss his works, but praise and bless the Creator in all things.
39.41: 39.41 And now in all his time. As if to say: Do not say the former times were better than now. Virtues make good days, vices bad.
40.2: 40.2 Thoughts. RABANUS. He enumerates the evils which man bears for sins.
40.6: 40.6 A little. Because the dead and insensible flesh seems to rest for a time, the soul already feels sorrow, and after the resurrection with its body will live in eternal punishments.
40.7: 40.7 Is troubled. THE SAME. Therefore the wicked will be tormented in punishment, etc., down to of the noble, namely, and the ignoble.
40.10: 40.10 And because of them the flood was made. To sinning man manifold punishment is assigned, that corrected he may repent, and afterward beware; but because he neglects, and grows in punishments, God brings a flood on the world to destroy the man he created. In comparison with the future punishment, what man suffers in the present is nothing.
40.11: 40.11 And all the waters. THE SAME. The works, namely, of sinners do not acquire the fruit of the heavenly reward, but the destruction of punishments.
40.13: 40.13 The substance of the unjust. They begin to bud, but waver in temptation, and suddenly wither at the first heat of persecution.
40.15: 40.15 The posterity of the wicked shall not bring forth many branches. We often see the progeny of the impious quickly fail, especially when the sons imitate the iniquity of the fathers.
40.18: 40.18 The life of one who is sufficient for himself. Sweet is the sleep of the laborer, whether he eat little or much. You shall find a treasure. For he truly proves himself a Christian who believes and does the commandments of Christ.
40.20: 40.20 Wine and music rejoice the heart. These naturally soothe and gladden the soul, but the love of wisdom and a tongue sweetly teaching strengthens the understanding much more.
40.22: 40.22 The eye desires favor and beauty. The ornament, namely, of the temple and diversity of worship, which the former people had under the law, the preaching of the Gospel sown in the world surpasses in the greenness of good works.
40.26: 40.26 Riches and strength. RABANUS. Riches given in the Lord, etc., down to both these and all the wealth of the world.
40.30: 40.30 A man looking. For it is foolish to be idle, and seek reward from another's labor. For every one shall receive according to his works.
40.32: 40.32 In the mouth of the imprudent poverty shall be trampled, etc. He who is pleased to be idly torpid, and by teaching to profit not his neighbors, at length shall burn with the pains of hell and late repentance.
41.1: 41.1 O death, etc. RABANUS. To him who loves the prosperity of the world and riches, bodily death is bitter, because he neglects the joys of the life to come.
41.5: 41.5 This judgment. THE SAME. It is common to all flesh, nor can anyone escape, though he live a hundred or a thousand years or more; whence: Who is the man that shall live, and not see death? Psalm 88.
41.8: 41.8 Children of abominations. Abominable are the children of sinners, who have imitated their impious fathers.
41.10: 41.10 Of an impious father. He who rears children ill, or destroys them by example, is guilty of their perdition. Or, he who begets evil works from a perverse will will be condemned for them.
41.13: 41.13 Into perdition. He answers the above, in which he discussed temporal death: because as man created from the earth for original sin returns to the earth, though to rise in incorruption; so the impious cursed for their sins shall go into eternal perdition with body and soul.
41.15: 41.15 Have a care of a good name, etc. That you live well and religiously. In this way a good name is acquired.
41.18: 41.18 Better is the man that hides his folly, etc. He that hides up corn shall be cursed among the people, but a blessing upon the head of them that sell.
41.19: 41.19 But yet return to those things that proceed. Because he foretold that a good name and a good life are useful, and reproved those hiding knowledge, he persuades them to return to the zeal for teaching, because it is not good to be irreverent and disobedient to one's teacher.
41.20: 41.20 It is not good to observe every shame. According to the letter, he instructs us to beware of vices, and give effort to virtues, and not, the better despised, choose the worse, which confusion everlasting follows.
41.26: 41.26 Turn not away your face from your neighbor, etc. RABANUS. When the angels shall gather out of the Church all scandals, etc., down to and has mingled with the fornications of heretics.
41.27: 41.27 Look not at another man's wife, etc. Carnal cupidity which ought to be subject to the spirit, we ought not to examine this and be subject to its suggestions.
42.1: 42.1 Do not double a speech, etc. RABANUS. He forbids to say good and evil together from the hidden of the heart; whence: Does a fountain send forth out of the same hole sweet and bitter water?
42.4: 42.4 Of the equality of the balance, etc. THE SAME. Equity is everywhere to be followed, etc., down to let us rule subjects also with discretion of discipline. Of the equality of the balance. How much hypocrisy and guile displease the Lord is shown by these words: A deceitful balance is an abomination before God. He who weighs the cause of the poor otherwise than of the mighty; or thinks his own errors lighter than those of others; or who lay upon the shoulders of men unbearable burdens; or who does good in public, evil in secret, is abominable to the Lord.
42.5: 42.5 And to a wicked servant. It signifies the servant who is not corrected by words must be restrained by blows. The servant of vices also is to be corrected by severe discipline.
42.7: 42.7 Where there are many hands, etc. He admonishes that where there are diverse wills gaping after spiritual gain, one must dispense cautiously. For some seek the word with the wish to tempt, others to learn, but not all things suit all.
42.8: 42.8 Of discipline. He who reproves each with fitting discipline shows himself a learned and approved teacher in the sight of the saints. Nor is youthful age to be despised in a teacher whom life and discretion commend.
42.9: 42.9 The daughter of the father. RABANUS. Mystically the daughter of the father, etc., down to or transgress the law of God, made barren in all good things. The daughter of the father. He teaches, literally, that parents take care of their offspring, and bring them up with discipline, and not loosen the reins to wantonness and pleasure.
42.11: 42.11 Over a wanton daughter, etc. Who requires a diligent watch. For if she is left to her own will, she confounds the teacher and makes him blush in the multitude of the people. Whence, dangerously he ministers to you whose face you frequently attend. For shameless eyes know not how to consider the beauty of the soul, but of bodies.
42.14: 42.14 For better is the iniquity of a man, etc. THE SAME. Woman either signifies the sex, etc., down to because she does things worthy of confusion.
42.15: 42.15 I will remember therefore the works, etc. THE SAME. Hitherto he has discussed diverse matters, etc., down to and afterward describes the mighty deeds of the fathers.
42.19: 42.19 For the Lord knew, etc. Because all ages of the world are present to him, with whom nothing is past, nothing future; he alone reveals mysteries, who knows the hearts of each, who looks upon all thoughts and words.
42.21: 42.21 The great works of his wisdom. When, namely, to the prophets and apostles he revealed the sacrament of his counsel hidden from ages and generations to the faithful. For he is before all, and after all, to whom nothing is added, nothing diminished.
42.23: 42.23 And as a spark. As a spark in the works of God we consider, because we scarcely receive a small knowledge thence.
42.25: 42.25 All things double, etc. RABANUS. So God ordained all things that what seem to be contrary agree, like the elements or the four seasons.
43.1: 43.1 Of height, etc. THE SAME. The beauty of the firmament, etc., down to no one with bodily eyes can bear the splendor of the divinity.
43.3: 43.3 Keeping the furnace. Because the proud, for thought, speech and evil working, eternal flame tortures.
43.5: 43.5 And in his words, etc. THE SAME. With mystical words he mocks the understanding of the proud. He hastened, etc. When in the preaching of the Gospel the way of salvation and the entrance of the heavenly kingdom is prepared.
43.6: 43.6 And the moon, etc. THE SAME. After he discussed the sun, etc., down to but is more rightly assigned to April, because in it it either begins, or ends, or is wholly included.
43.7: 43.7 A luminary that is diminished, etc. The moon has no native splendor, but receives from the sun: so also the Church from Christ, which in persecution seems to be diminished, but in part grows bright; for she increases wonderfully in the consummation.
43.9: 43.9 A vessel of the camp, etc. Because in her consists the multitude of the faithful, which in the firmament of truth and of divine preaching shines gloriously through the whole world.
43.10: 43.10 The beauty of heaven, etc. The ornament of the Church, the fullness of the saints, whom God Most High ordained to illumine by preaching the Gospel. These, abiding in holy words and in the doctrine of true faith, await the judgment of God.
43.11: 43.11 In the words. Because in their patience they possess their souls, girded about the loins; and holding lamps in their hands, they wait for their Lord, when he shall return from the wedding.
43.12: 43.12 See the bow, etc. The writing of the Old or New Testament. This to the faithful shows a sweet yoke, to the stubborn terrible arms.
43.13: 43.13 It has compassed heaven, etc. When through the power and wisdom of God, that is Christ, the Old and New Testament was established.
43.16: 43.16 And the stones of the hail were broken. Teachers, who water the earth of the human heart, and bear in themselves the storm of reproof, and pour it forth in due time, and break the stones of hail; by rebuking, namely, the hardness of the perverse heart they stone the living grass.
43.17: 43.17 The south wind shall blow. RABANUS. Which is also the Auster, etc., down to the powerful to the persecution of the Christian name, and sometimes to penance.
43.18: 43.18 The tempest. God inflicts various trials through malignant spirits, to make the fervor of faith and love grow cold.
43.21: 43.21 The frost like salt, etc. That is, barrenness; for where salt is scattered, barrenness follows: the devil by the cold of unbelief makes earthly hearts barren for good works.
43.24: 43.24 The remedy, etc. All eloquence fails in comparison with him, nor suffices to tell his power.
43.26: 43.26 They that sail on the sea, etc. There are many dangers of the sea literally, and there wonderful works of God in various beasts, as writers on natural things have handed down. In the sea also of this world there are many monsters of demons and many snares of theirs.
43.34: 43.34 Be not weary, etc. RABANUS. To comprehend what is incomprehensible. Whence seek not riches which you cannot reach.
44.1: 44.1 Let us praise men, etc. Discoursing morally, and touching allegory and anagoge in most places, he brought forth the mysteries of the divine sacrament; now he begins to relate of the holy fathers. Our parents. The patriarchs, who enjoyed divine speech and vision; and the Prophets, who, filled with the Holy Spirit, foretold many mysteries of Christ and the Church.
44.12: 44.12 In the covenants stood, etc. RABANUS. These according to the history of the patriarchs, etc., down to when the seed of good works will be compensated by the heavenly reward.
44.16: 44.16 Enoch pleased God. Not from Adam, etc., down to to give men counsel of repenting.
44.17: 44.17 Noah was found, etc. When the world perishing by the flood, he was preserved, to preach penance to the nations, and show by example that those who devoutly serve God are freed from eternal destruction. With him God made a covenant, that he would no more destroy all flesh with the waters of the flood, Genesis 17. It signifies the rulers, who amid the waves of the world govern the ark, that is the Church, and preach the baptism of penance, appeasing God for the human race by prayers and sacrifices.
44.21: 44.21 In his flesh he made the covenant to stand, etc. RABANUS. That it might be signified our nature renewed through the baptism of Christ, after the putting off of the old man.
44.22: 44.22 Therefore by an oath, etc. The promise to Abraham is double. In the sand of the sea the barren Jews are expressed; in the likeness of the stars, the faithful Christians, who shall shine with the light of the resurrection as the stars of heaven.
44.26: 44.26 And he gave him an inheritance, etc. Of the Gentile people, who later came to the grace of faith and the regeneration of baptism, to whom the fullness of the paternal blessing came.
45.6: 45.6 Precepts. On Mount Sinai, namely, he gave him the law and the precepts of life, speaking with him in a cloud.
45.9: 45.9 And he girded him, etc. He describes the rite of the old priesthood and the ornament of the high priest, all of which were a figure of the New Testament, and of the true priest Jesus Christ. And clothed. The garments of the priest are the works of virtues: wisdom, doctrine.
45.14: 45.14 A crown of gold, etc. In which was the name of the almighty God, which signifies the honor of the divine majesty, since above all things we ought to set, that in all our acts and words God be honored through Jesus Christ, who is our head, 1 Peter 4.
45.17: 45.17 Sacrifices. RABANUS. How Moses Aaron, etc., down to for the priesthood of Christ and the rite of sacrifices will remain forever.
45.28: 45.28 Phinees the son of Eleazar. THE SAME. Phinees, as it is written in the book of Numbers, Chapter 25, etc., down to he happily came to the mountain of strength, that is Christ.
45.31: 45.31 And the covenant of David. THE SAME. It signifies that David in the distribution of the ministries of God, etc., down to and in the tabernacle he ordered the turns of the ministers.
46.1: 46.1 Valiant in war, Joshua the son of Nun. RABANUS. Jesus in work and word signifies Christ, etc., down to triumphing over principalities and powers in himself.
46.4: 46.4 Who before him, etc. THE SAME. How in the meeting of Joshua the sun was stayed, etc., down to will be shortened in the time of destruction.
46.9: 46.9 From sins. Of despair, when, hearing the reports of the spies, they despaired of entering the land.
46.13: 46.13 And the judges every one, etc. RABANUS. After Joshua, there succeeded judges who defended the people of God from enemies; and after the passion of Christ, the apostles rulers of the Church of God.
46.14: 46.14 That their memory may be, etc. Because they persevered in right faith, that their memory be confirmed by perpetual blessing. Bones. The strength of good works is given reward, that the memory of their name be passed to posterity with glory.
46.16: 46.16 Beloved of the Lord, etc. RABANUS. History relates that the Lord to the child Samuel, etc., down to he pronounces to wicked rulers future punishment and perpetual death.
47.1: 47.1 After these things Nathan rose up. Literally, he recalls the deeds of David, of which the book of Kings and Paralipomenon relate most fully.
47.2: 47.2 As the fat. It signifies that he filled with the grace of the Holy Spirit, was separated from the fellowship of the carnal in life and manners.
47.3: 47.3 He played with lions. RABANUS. David signifies Christ, etc., down to and gave him a name which is above every name.
47.14: 47.14 After him rose up a wise son. THE SAME. Mystically, Solomon, etc., down to as in one threshing floor the grains signify the good, the chaff the wicked.
47.23: 47.23 That you may make an empire, etc. THE SAME. Because ten tribes followed Jeroboam, and two Rehoboam; Jeroboam was of Ephraim, who first reigned cruelly over the ten tribes.
47.27: 47.27 And he left behind him, etc. THE SAME. Mystically, Rehoboam, who is interpreted breadth of the people, etc., down to remained in the rule of Catholic faith.
47.28: 47.28 He turned away the people by his counsel. Believing, namely, the counsel of the young men.
48.1: 48.1 And Elijah rose up. RABANUS. Who burned two captains of fifty sent by king Ahaziah with fire from heaven, 4 Kings 1.
48.2: 48.2 Who brought. THE SAME. Mystically, the three years' famine figured the famine of the word of God and of faith in the Trinity, etc., down to that afterward might come he who neither translated nor carried up, would pierce the ethereal heaven by his own power.
48.13: 48.13 Elijah indeed in a whirlwind, etc. THE SAME. Since the disciple is not above the master, etc., down to for he who with firm faith touches the death of Christ, is partaker of his resurrection. In Elisha filled. Who prayed the day: Let your spirit be double in me, and obtained. Whence he was invincible in patience and virtue, who in life and in death did many signs.
48.17: 48.17 There was left a very small people. Because the house of David, and the tribe of Judah, and Benjamin, did not altogether cast off the worship of God, but some of them were idolaters, like Joram and Ahaz: others clave to God, like Hezekiah and Josiah.
48.19: 48.19 Hezekiah fortified his city, etc. RABANUS. That Hezekiah stops the fountain, etc., down to the city freed, the enemies being destroyed, is fully shown in Paralipomenon.
49.1: 49.1 The memory of Josiah. RABANUS. The memory of king Josiah, etc., down to he himself with zeal for God cleanses the land of Judah and Jerusalem from all abominations, who says: The zeal of your house has eaten me up.
49.5: 49.5 Except David, and Hezekiah, and Josiah, etc. These three in comparison with others are not said to have sinned. For what they sinned they blotted out by worthy penance, and pleased God by devotion and piety.
49.8: 49.8 They set on fire the chosen city of holiness, etc. THE SAME. Some understand this place in the person of Christ, etc., down to these destroyed, he built the Church of God.
49.10: 49.10 Ezekiel who saw, etc. THE SAME. Mystically, Ezekiel, etc., down to and foretold remedies to the penitent.
49.11: 49.11 In the rain. It signifies that he preached that the rain of vengeance would come upon sinners, and promised the consolation of mercy to those walking in the way of the commandments of God.
49.13: 49.13 For he also, etc. Because it signifies Christ, who is the image of God: that whoever believes in God, may be as it were sealed with a ring.
49.14: 49.14 And Jesus the son of Josedec. Because by the grace of Jesus Christ, who is our king and priest, after the captivity of diabolical oppression, the Church is rebuilt.
49.15: 49.15 Nehemiah. RABANUS. God the Consoler, or consoled by the Lord, etc., down to who builds the city of God, that is the Church, and consoles the sorrowing.
49.16: 49.16 No man, etc. Enoch, dedication. This signifies Christ, who built and consecrated the Church with his blood; who came into the world without sin, and with glory will be taken up into heaven.
49.17: 49.17 As Joseph. Joseph, like Jacob his father, desired the land of promise, detested Egypt; teaching us to desire the land of the living, that we may rest in peace.
49.18: 49.18 And his bones were visited. RABANUS. It signifies that Joseph, etc., down to and buried in Sichem, which is Neapolis, a city of the Samaritans.
49.19: 49.19 Seth and Shem, etc. Seth the son of Adam, and Shem the firstborn of Noah, were set above the men of their time as much by faith as by manners; in whom Christ is signified, who is God and man.
50.1: 50.1 Simon the son of Onias. RABANUS. He came to men in his time, etc., down to since Jesus describes the life and manners of Simon so expressly.
50.3: 50.3 Wells of waters. The depths of the Scriptures, which lie hid in the divine books under figures, but overflow by the mouth of preachers, like the sea to the satisfying of very many.
50.5: 50.5 And he enlarged the entrance of the house of the court. Because in the unlearned, whom the court signifies; and in the perfect, who are signified by the house, the merit of the masters increases.
50.11: 50.11 In putting on the robe, etc. The order of preachers, by putting on the robe of glory, and clothing themselves with the consummation of virtues, shows the judgment of their dignity, and the ornament of faith, and the clothing of good working. For these ought to appear in priests, that they may worthily teach.
50.13: 50.13 And in receiving the portions from the hand of the priest. He receives portions from the hand of the priest, who exacts the act of good working from the ministers.
50.15: 50.15 And finishing at the altar. The finished offering is given to the high King, when the body of Christ is offered to God.
50.17: 50.17 He poured out at the foot. In commemoration of Christ, who is the foundation of the Church, of this oblation is a most sweet odor to Almighty God.
50.18: 50.18 Then the sons of Aaron shouted. The priests of Christ showed forth preaching through the passion consummated. The ductile trumpets are well said, because preachers grow as much as they are struck by the hammers of tribulations.
50.19: 50.19 Then all the people, etc. When the ecclesiastical office is performed by the ministers of the altar in memory of Christ, the people, provoked to the praise of God, prostrate on their face, that is, show the humility of their heart. To give prayers to the Almighty. Because whatever is done for the love of God is before God prayer and an odor of sweetness; because the whole Church strives to persevere in prayer until the end of the world, when the body of Christ will be honored in incorruption, and the members joined to their head.
50.21: 50.21 And the people prayed, etc. RABANUS. Because whatever is offered to God in the unity of faith is received with him; whatever outside, is reckoned to impiety. A great sound is made in the Church, when to the praying and blessing priests the whole people answers: Amen: which sound pertains as much to the cry of the voice as to the devotion of the heart.
50.22: 50.22 Then descending, etc. The company of the saints exulting. He lifted up. When he gives thanks for the perfection of labor in the salvation of all the people, then he multiplies praises, repeats prayer, because he never ceases from praises.
50.23: 50.23 To show the power of God. To preach, namely, the mercy of him who gives us joy of heart, and peace in eternal times, that all the men of Israel, and lovers of the eternal King, may preach the power and goodness of God in the deliverance of his people.
50.27: 50.27 Two nations, etc. A double ruin, the Gentiles, namely, who are polluted with idolatry and vain conversation.
50.29: 50.29 The doctrine of wisdom, etc. He commends his work, showing how useful it is to the one who reads, meditates and does.
51.1: 51.1 The prayer of Jesus the son of Sirach. It is better referred to the whole Church than to one person, because in her many kinds of tribulations and diverse consolations are described. I will give thanks to you, O Lord, King. RABANUS. Jesus Christ is the helper and protector of his bride, who delivered himself up for her, that he might free her from the perdition of original sin.
51.5: 51.5 From the gates of tribulations. These are the mouths of princes and tyrants, whence threats and deceits proceed, which compel the servants of God to deny the faith.
51.6: 51.6 From the oppression of the flame. This happened to the three children in the furnace of fire bodily; but all the saints are freed spiritually from the heat of persecution.
51.9: 51.9 And my life was drawing near to hell. Because the life of the flesh by daily failing tends to death. For he calls death hell, because the death of the flesh is the vengeance of the first sin, as hell is the perpetual punishment of sinning souls.
51.10: 51.10 They compassed me on every side, etc. The Church seeing herself surrounded by enemies, and human consolation lacking, seeks help from God, from whom is all good, to whom she ascribes that she is delivered from enemies.
